question.text: Under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, which of the following is correct with respect to an AIF Investment Manager and its designated persons?

answer.text: PIT Regulations apply only to listed companies and their promoters; AIFs are outside scope
PIT applies only if the AIF has more than 50% holding in a listed investee company
Only the Compliance Officer of the AIF is bound by PIT; fund managers and analysts are exempt

An AIF and its designated persons can be 'deemed connected persons' due to potential access to UPSI about listed investee companies; Board must adopt an Internal Code of Conduct, maintain a structured digital database of UPSI recipients (with PAN) preserved for at least 8 years, enforce Chinese Walls and pre-clearance

explanation.text: The Logic: PIT Regulation 2(1)(d) covers connected persons; Regulation 3 governs communication/procurement of UPSI; Regulation 4 governs trading-when-in-possession. An AIF with frequent communication with listed-investee officers is 'deemed connected'. Regulation 9/9A mandates the Code of Conduct for designated persons. Regulation 3(5) (w.e.f. 17 July 2020 amendment) requires structured digital database with PAN, preserved at least 8 years. The Trap: Options A and B dangerously underscope PIT. Option C ignores that all designated persons (CIO, PMs, analysts, IR) are covered — not just Compliance. Cross-Exam Context: XV (Research Analyst) tests PIT from research angle. XIX-C tests Manager application. XXI-B (PM) covers designated-persons framework. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: Pre-clearance threshold in the Code of Conduct must be set consciously (typical market: > INR 10 lakh). Trades must be executed within 7 trading days of approval. Window-closure for trading must sync with investee earnings calendar. The structured digital database must NOT be outsourced.
